correctness.rationale: Restoring the deleted perfect matching turns the crown into K_{n,n}; feasibility is preserved under that edge addition, so the published value four for K_{n,n} is a lower bound. A same-index pair labeled two gives a feasible crown function of weight four. At equality, zeros on both sides force side totals two; the exact neighborhood inequality then forces matched zero coordinates on both sides, and total weight two per side forces identical vectors of sum two. The restrained zero-subgraph condition holds exactly in the stated range. The bundled exhaustive checker confirms the complete classification for n=4,5,6.

value.rationale: Crown graphs are the canonical perfect-matching deletion of K_{n,n}, making them a natural robustness test for a domination invariant already known exactly on complete bipartite graphs. The theorem proves numerical stability under the structured deletion while exposing a new synchronization law for every optimum function and gives the exact minimum-function multiplicity.
